Wikipedia coverage states CoreSite was established in 2001 as CRG West, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. In May 2007 the company acquired Santa Clara land for a planned 50 megawatt data center as part of a wider expansion that also added Boston and Chicago properties. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. As of June 2022 CoreSite operated 27 data center facilities across 10 markets totaling over 4.6 million net rentable square feet, with Los Angeles and San Francisco/San Jose/Santa Clara both listed among its key markets. American Tower completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. No building specific address or individual MW figures for these particular registry rows were located in available sourcing this session.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] CoreSite was founded in 2001 as CRG West, a Carlyle Group portfolio company, beginning operations at two West Coast carrier hotel buildings, Market Post Tower and One Wilshire, both in Los Angeles. The firm rebranded from CRG West to CoreSite in June 2009 and completed an IPO in September 2010. American Tower Corporation, the public tower and infrastructure company (NYSE: AMT, SEC CIK 1053507), completed its acquisition of CoreSite in December 2021. Stonepeak Partners LP later bought roughly 29 percent of American Towers US data center business directly in July 2022, increasing that stake to about 36 percent by October 2022. CoreSites own current Silicon Valley regional page (operator source, tier-1, https://www.coresite.com/data-center-locations/silicon-valley) names nine data centers on this Santa Clara campus, SV1 through SV9, totaling more than 1.4 million square feet campus wide, but only describes SV1, SV2, SV4, SV7, SV8, and SV9 individually, SV1 and SV2 are not rows in this registry. SV3, SV5, and SV6 are not detailed on that page, so their building specific facts below come from data center industry aggregator directories instead. This specific building, SV3, is one of the three Silicon Valley buildings the operators own regional page names but does not detail individually. Baxtel, DataCenterMap, Inflect, datacenterHawk, Ocolo, and Datacenters.com independently agree this buildings address is 2901 Coronado Drive, Santa Clara, CA 95054, a strong multi source aggregator agreement even though the operator itself does not publish this address at the individual building level. Baxtel lists this building at approximately 50,000 square feet, though its own building versus gross square footage columns for this campus appear inconsistently labeled across buildings, so this figure is treated as approximate rather than precise. No MW or power capacity figure was found for this specific building in any source checked this session.

reading:
CoreSite traces to 2001, when it was founded as CRG West, a Carlyle Group portfolio company, before rebranding as CoreSite in 2009. American Tower Corporation, the public tower and infrastructure company trading as AMT, SEC filer CIK 1053507, completed its acquisition of CoreSite in late 2021. Stonepeak Partners LP later bought into American Tower's US data center business directly, acquiring roughly 29 percent in July 2022 and increasing that stake to about 36 percent by October 2022.

CoreSite's own site describes a portfolio of 30 data centers across 11 US markets, Atlanta, Boston, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Miami, New York, Northern Virginia, Orlando, Raleigh, Silicon Valley, and Washington DC, totaling more than 4.8 million square feet, with more than 44,000 customer interconnections and 500 or more connected network providers. The company remains headquartered in Denver, Colorado, where American Tower has continued building new CoreSite capacity, including a 180,000-square-foot DE3 facility reported under construction in Denver.

The registry here tracks 19 CoreSite facilities across six states plus Washington DC, California, the District of Columbia, Georgia, Illinois, New Jersey, and Virginia, a subset of CoreSite's 11 named markets. As with Equinix, CoreSite's model concentrates in major metro interconnection hubs rather than large single-campus buildouts, and its ownership structure, a REIT-like data center subsidiary carved out under a publicly traded tower company with a private-capital minority partner in Stonepeak, is a distinct financing pattern from the wholly private-equity buyouts recorded for QTS, CyrusOne, and Flexential elsewhere in this registry.
